To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FK-506 and cyclosporin (CsA) inhibit transcription of the IL-2 gene, and that the degree of inhibition is related to the amount of transcription induced by T-cell activation.

(i) the immunosuppressants FK-506 and cyclosporin (CsA) specifically inhibit the transcriptional activation induced in T cells by the IL- 2 promoter elements NFAT1 and NF-IL-2A; and (ii) the degree to which FK-506 or CSa inhibits a given promoter element correlates with the degree to which the promoter element is induced upon T-cell stimulation.
FK-506 inhibits mitogen-stimulated transcription of the IL-2 gene by blocking the activation of the IL- 2 enhancer elements NF-AT and NFIL- 2A.
